app.name: HubSpot Developer Platform app (Projects-based OAuth app)

verdict.summary: Creating your own OAuth app and connecting your own account is quick and needs no review. Wider use is limited by HubSpot install caps (25 unlisted Marketplace installs, 10 allowlisted private accounts), and removing those caps requires a Marketplace listing review by HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team; certification is a further, optional, multi-month review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 2-4 hours for Gates 1 and 2 (including up to 48 hours of DNS wait for a verified domain). Listing preparation adds roughly a day or more of content and scope work, plus the review wait.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under about 1 hour once the HubSpot CLI (v7.6.0 or later) and a developer account are in place (estimate; not stated in the findings).
verdict.approval_wait: None for Gates 1 and 2. Marketplace listing: initial review within 10 business days; full review and feedback up to 60 days from when feedback is shared. Certification adds at least six months of listing (reported as a requirement, not a review time).

gates.name: Developer account and test install (works for you)
gates.unlocks: Your own OAuth app with its own client ID and secret, connected to your own developer test account. No review.
limits: Installs in developer test accounts show the unverified-app checkbox that must be ticked before Connect app.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes and must be refreshed from the refresh token.
The app does not appear as a Connected App in an account until the refresh and initial access tokens are generated.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes to about 1 hour, once the CLI is installed.

gates.name: Private distribution and unlisted Marketplace install (works for invited or test users)
gates.unlocks: Installs in your own standard account and in up to 10 allowlisted private accounts (not counting developer test accounts), or unlisted Marketplace installs up to 25 installs.
limits: Privately distributed OAuth apps: up to 10 allowlisted accounts, not counting developer test accounts.
Unlisted Marketplace OAuth apps: capped at 25 installs until listed on the Marketplace.
Installers see an unverified-app warning and must type an acceptance phrase unless the app is verified (a verified domain removes the unverified banner).
Before installing in any account other than a developer test account, you must review and sign the Acceptable Use Policy from the Distribution tab.
Installers must be a Super Admin, or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access plus the permission for each requested scope group.
Only one verified domain per developer account.
Per-app burst limits apply: 100 per 10 seconds on Free/Starter, 190 on Professional/Enterprise, 250 with the API Limit Increase.
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1, plus up to 48 hours if you add a verified domain.

gates.name: Marketplace listing (works for anyone on the Marketplace)
gates.unlocks: Public Marketplace listing with no 25-install cap after listing. Listing is a review of the listing, not a general app-store review of every install. Certification is a separate, optional step on top of listing.
limits: Listing requires at least three active, unique HubSpot production installs unaffiliated with you, with activity in the past 30 days.
Listing requires OAuth as the sole authorization method, a unique app per use case, and no redirect to another app.

Listing requires every requested scope to be used, live privacy policy and terms of service URLs, live setup documentation, a working install button URL, a support contact, and a Shared data table matching the scopes.
Apps must run on a supported Developer Platform version (Projects 2025.2 or later, 2026.03 recommended).
HubSpot may unpublish or refuse a listing at any time; only one app can be submitted at a time.

Certification (optional): verified domain, listed at least six months, at least 60 active unaffiliated installs, demo video, security questionnaire, and reliability above 95%. Certification is free and lasts two years.
gates.time_to_reach: Requires at least three active production installs first, then listing preparation and an initial review within 10 business days.

steps.title: Check developer account access and avoid legacy app types
steps.detail: Sign in to a HubSpot account with access to the Development menu, and confirm you are a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access for installs. Do not use a legacy private app: creation of new legacy private apps was disabled on October 26, 2026 for existing accounts, so create a Projects-based app instead.
gotchas: Legacy private app creation is closed as of today (2026-10-28); existing legacy private apps keep working until September 2027.
Legacy public apps created before June 23, 2026 must move to Projects-based apps.

steps.title: Install the HubSpot CLI and create the project app
steps.detail: Install HubSpot CLI v7.6.0 or later, then run hs project create. Choose the distribution (Marketplace or restricted to specific accounts) and the auth type OAuth.
gotchas: CLI v7.6.0 is the stated minimum for the 2025.2 and 2026.03 platform.
Pick the distribution now; it determines which install limits apply (see Gate 2).

steps.title: Set the redirect URI in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: Add the callback URL to the redirectUrls field in app-hsmeta.json, then run hs project upload. The agent can make this edit and validate the URL format (https, domain name, exact match) before upload.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Production redirect URLs must use https; http is only for localhost testing.
IP addresses are not supported, and the URL must match the registered value exactly.
Composio's callback is Composio's own URL, not one you control.

steps.title: Trim the scope list
steps.detail: Edit requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes in app-hsmeta.json (or check scopes on the Auth tab) so they list only what your agent actually uses. Any scope checked there is treated as required. The agent can draft the list from your use cases and flag scopes that are not used.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list is broad (for example settings.users.write and many CRM read/write scopes). Remove what you do not need, because listing requires every requested scope to be used.
Sensitive Data scopes are not in Composio's default list and require Enterprise plus approval from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team.

steps.title: Copy client ID and client secret into Composio
steps.detail: Run hs project open, open the project's app component, and go to the Auth tab. Copy the Client ID and Client secret from Client credentials, and enter them in your Composio auth config. The secret can be rotated from the same Auth tab if it is exposed.
gotchas: Composio's managed app is a different client ID; using your own app means Composio uses your credentials, not its managed app.
Managed auth does not lift HubSpot's install limits.

steps.title: Run a test install in a developer test account
steps.detail: In Development > Test accounts, create a developer test account. Open the project's Distribution tab, add a test install, select the unverified-app checkbox, and click Connect app. Then complete the Composio connection flow.

values.label: Install path
values.value: Development > Test accounts, then Distribution tab > test install

gotchas: Your app appears as a Connected App only after the refresh and initial access tokens are generated.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; test the refresh path, not only the first token.

steps.title: Install in your own standard account
steps.detail: On the Distribution tab, under Standard install, click Install now to install in your own standard account. You must be a Super Admin or hold Marketplace Access.
gotchas: Installing in accounts other than developer test accounts requires the Acceptable Use Policy to be signed first (Gate 2 step).

steps.title: Add a verified domain
steps.detail: In Development, open the Domain page and add your domain. Publish the DNS TXT record HubSpot gives you and wait for verification. This removes the unverified-app banner for installers. Only one verified domain is allowed per developer account.
steps.est_time: 15 min setup; up to 48 hours propagation
gotchas: Verification usually completes within an hour, but DNS propagation can take up to 48 hours.
Without a verified domain, installers see the unverified banner.

steps.title: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy
steps.detail: Open the Distribution tab and click Begin publishing. Review and sign the Acceptable Use Policy. Until this is signed, you cannot install the app in accounts other than developer test accounts. This is a legal acceptance only you can do.
gotchas: Signing is required even for private distribution to allowlisted accounts.

steps.title: Allowlist private accounts or set up unlisted install
steps.detail: For private distribution, allowlist up to 10 accounts (not counting developer test accounts). For an unlisted Marketplace app, plan for a cap of 25 installs and an unverified warning. Each installer must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access and each scope group permission. The exact allowlist UI is not in the findings; confirm it in the Distribution tab.
gotchas: Private OAuth allowlist can be raised for Solutions Partners (reported up to 100), but this is not confirmed on an official page.
Per-account burst limit is 110 requests per 10 seconds for Marketplace apps on 2025.2 or 2026.03; the API limit increase add-on does not raise it.

steps.title: Implement token refresh by expiry, not 401
steps.detail: Make the token exchange a POST to /oauth/v3/token with grant_type authorization_code. Refresh the access token based on expires_in and the 30-minute lifetime. Do not treat a 401 as the signal to fetch a new token. Confirm with Composio whether its managed connection handles refresh for your app.
gotchas: Refresh token lifetime and PKCE support are not confirmed in the findings.
Certification also requires refresh without user involvement and calling Uninstall App when a customer removes the app.

steps.title: Decide whether to list on the Marketplace
steps.detail: Listing is optional. Before you apply, confirm you have at least three active, unique production installs unaffiliated with you, using OAuth. Confirm the app is OAuth-only, uses every requested scope, and runs on Projects 2025.2 or later (2026.03 recommended). Projects 2025.1 reached end of support on August 1, 2026, and its builds fail.
gotchas: The listing-submit button is reported to stay disabled until three active installs exist (community report).
Apps on 2025.1 cannot be listed.

steps.title: Draft listing content
steps.detail: Draft the public setup documentation, privacy policy, terms of service, pricing statement, support contact, install button URL, and Shared data table matching your scopes. The agent can draft these from your scope list and product description. You must review the legal text and publish it at live URLs.
gotchas: Privacy policy and terms of service URLs must be live and up to date.
The Shared data table must match the scopes requested exactly.

steps.title: Submit the listing and wait for review
steps.detail: Submit the listing from the app's listing settings and wait for HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team. The initial review takes up to 10 business days. Only one app can be submitted at a time. Missing key fields send the listing to Draft.
steps.est_time: 30 min to submit; up to 10 business days initial review
gotchas: Full review and feedback can take up to 60 days from when feedback is shared.
HubSpot can unpublish or refuse a listing at any time under the Marketplace terms.

steps.title: Wait for provider review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews the listing. Respond promptly to feedback, because the 60-day review clock runs from when feedback is shared. Certification is a separate later application and is not needed for listing.
steps.est_time: up to 10 business days initial; up to 60 days full review
gotchas: Certification requires at least six months of listing, a verified domain, 60 active unaffiliated installs, a demo video, and a security questionnaire.
HubSpot can reject a certification request at its discretion; an unsuccessful app may re-apply after six months.

requirements.item: Developer account with Development menu access
requirements.detail: You need a HubSpot account with access to Development to create the project app, test accounts and Domain page.

requirements.item: Super Admin or Marketplace Access to install
requirements.detail: Installers must be a Super Admin, or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access plus permission for each requested scope group.
Required before installing in any account other than developer test accounts. Signed from Distribution tab > Begin publishing.
Add the domain under Development > Domain and publish a DNS TXT record. Removes the unverified banner. One per developer account.

requirements.item: Install caps for unlisted or private apps
requirements.detail: Unlisted Marketplace OAuth apps: 25 installs. Privately distributed OAuth apps: up to 10 allowlisted accounts, not counting developer test accounts.

requirements.item: OAuth as the only authorization method
requirements.detail: Marketplace listing requires OAuth as the sole authorization method, with a unique app per use case and no redirect to another app.

requirements.item: Three active production installs unaffiliated with you
requirements.detail: Counted as unique production accounts with successful OAuth API activity or signed webhook/card requests in the past 30 days.

requirements.item: Use every requested scope; remove unused ones
requirements.detail: Listing requires that the app use all scopes requested at install.
Live public setup documentation, live privacy policy and terms of service URLs, working install button URL, a support contact, accurate pricing, and a Shared data table matching the scopes.
Apps must run on Projects 2025.2 or later (2026.03 recommended). Projects 2025.1 fails builds after its end of support on August 1, 2026.

requirements.item: Agree to Technology Partner Program Agreement; avoid restricted industries and classic CRM cards
requirements.detail: Listing rules also require agreement to the Technology Partner Program Agreement and avoiding restricted industries and classic CRM cards.

requirements.item: Certification: verified domain, six months listed, 60 installs, demo video, security questionnaire
requirements.detail: Optional, separate review. Demo video is required before review; security questionnaire covers encryption, access controls and OAuth token lifecycle.

scopes.effect: Requires an Enterprise account and a request to HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, which allowlists them for testing before publication. Existing users must re-authorize after sensitive scopes are added. Agent tools and UI cards on the Marketplace must not request them.
A second tier on top of sensitive scopes that needs additional scopes. Treat as sensitive and request separately.
Included in Composio's default list. Remove unless your agent needs to write user settings, because listing requires all requested scopes to be used.

scopes.scope: Broad CRM read/write scopes in Composio's default list (for example crm.objects.contacts.write, crm.objects.deals.write)
scopes.effect: Trim to scopes your agent uses. Scopes not used are not allowed on a listed app. The findings do not assign a tier to these scopes; the full scopes reference was not fetched.

A community post says the May 2026 certification review checks for one API call per declared scope in the trailing 30 days. This is not on the official page, which says extraneous scopes must be removed. Treat as unverified.

blockers.symptom: Installs stop at 25 on a Marketplace OAuth app you have not listed.
blockers.cause: Apps created or migrated to Developer Platform 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until listed on the Marketplace.
blockers.fix: Use private distribution for a small set of accounts, or submit a Marketplace listing (requires three active installs first). After listing, installs are unlimited.

blockers.symptom: Private distribution refuses more than 10 accounts.
blockers.cause: Privately distributed OAuth apps are limited to 10 allowlisted accounts, not counting developer test accounts. Static token apps are limited to one standard account.
blockers.fix: Keep to 10 allowlisted accounts, use OAuth rather than a static token if you need more, or pursue a listing. A Solutions Partner override is reported but not confirmed on an official page.

blockers.symptom: Installers see an unverified-app warning and must type an acceptance phrase.
blockers.cause: The app has not been verified by the Ecosystem Quality team, and no verified domain is set.
blockers.fix: Add and verify a domain under Development > Domain. Listing and review by the Ecosystem Quality team are needed to remove the banner entirely.

blockers.symptom: Cannot install in a real customer account; only test accounts work.
blockers.cause: The Acceptable Use Policy has not been signed.
blockers.fix: Open the Distribution tab and click Begin publishing, then review and sign the AUP.

blockers.symptom: Sensitive contact data scopes cannot be used, or the app fails on sensitive data.
blockers.cause: Sensitive Data scopes require an Enterprise subscription and approval from the Ecosystem Quality team.
blockers.fix: Confirm the account is Enterprise, request the scopes from Ecosystem Quality, and avoid sensitive scopes entirely if you plan a Marketplace listing for agent tools or UI cards.
blockers.contact: HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team (channel not stated in the findings)

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected or listing submit is disabled.
blockers.cause: Fewer than three active, unique, unaffiliated production installs with recent OAuth activity, or an app on an unsupported Developer Platform version (2025.1).
blockers.fix: Reach three active installs first, and move the project to Projects 2025.2 or 2026.03.

blockers.symptom: Legacy private app creation is blocked.
blockers.cause: HubSpot disabled new legacy private app creation (new accounts from September 28, 2026; existing accounts from October 26, 2026).
blockers.fix: Create a Projects-based app with hs project create instead. Service Keys in Projects 2026.09 are the stated replacement (release-note claim, not verified on an official page).

blockers.symptom: API calls get throttled for a customer account.
blockers.cause: Per-account limit of 110 requests every 10 seconds for Marketplace OAuth apps on 2025.2 or 2026.03; the API limit increase add-on does not raise it.
blockers.fix: Batch requests and back off on 429 responses. Do not treat 401 as a refresh trigger.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth app for a quick first connection; it needs no HubSpot app registration. Register your own app when you need your own client ID, a Marketplace listing, certification, or distribution beyond the install caps. Managed auth does not lift HubSpot's install limits. Composio's default scope list is broad, so trim to needed scopes before any listing. Composio's redirect is Composio's own callback, not one you control. Whether the 25-install cap applies to Composio's managed app is not confirmed.

evidence.claim: Marketplace OAuth apps are capped at 25 installs until HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews and lists them; after listing, installs are unlimited.
evidence.quote: Until your app is reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and listed on the Marketplace, you'll be limited to 25 installs.

evidence.claim: Listing content requirements: live public setup documentation, live privacy policy and terms of service URLs, a working install button URL, at least one support contact method, accurate pricing, and a Shared data table matching the scopes requested.
evidence.quote: URLs for your app's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy must be live and up-to-date.

evidence.claim: Listing review: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team does a manual initial review within 10 business days; the full review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared; only one app can be submitted at a time.
evidence.quote: the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days.

evidence.claim: HubSpot may unpublish or refuse a listing at any time under the Marketplace terms; listing submissions missing key fields are set to Draft mode.
evidence.quote: HubSpot reserves the right to unpublish or refuse publication of your app listing at any time.

evidence.claim: Apps on a developer platform version that has been announced as unsupported cannot be listed; the spring 2026 changelog says apps submitting for listing or certification must run on a supported version (Projects 2025.2 or later, with 2026.03 recommended).
evidence.quote: Marketplace apps that submit for listing/relisting or certification/recertification must run on a supported Developer Platform version

evidence.claim: Projects 2025.1 reached end of support on August 1, 2026, and builds on 2025.1 fail, so apps must move to 2025.2 or 2026.03.
evidence.quote: Projects version 2025.1 reaches the end of support; builds on 2025.1 will fail

evidence.claim: Marketplace certification is a separate, optional review by the Ecosystem Quality team of security, privacy, reliability, performance, usability, accessibility and value; it requires OAuth, all required scopes, and a verified domain.
evidence.quote: App certification involves the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team reviewing and confirming that your listed app meets the requirements below

evidence.claim: Certification requires the listed public app to be on a verified domain, and the app must have been listed on the Marketplace for at least six months before it can be certified.
evidence.quote: Your app must be listed in the HubSpot Marketplace for at least six months.

evidence.claim: Certification requires at least 60 active, unique, unaffiliated installs to qualify for and keep certification; with fewer than three active installs the app may be removed from the Marketplace.
evidence.quote: Your app must have at least 60 active, unique installs to qualify for and retain certification.

evidence.claim: Certification requires a demo video submission before HubSpot will review the app, plus a security questionnaire covering encryption, access controls and OAuth token lifecycle, and a security best-practices assessment of public assets.
evidence.quote: HubSpot will not review your app unless you submit a demo video as instructed when applying for app certification.

evidence.claim: Certification security section: the app must pass a security best-practices assessment, and the developer must complete a questionnaire on encryption, access controls and token lifecycle management for OAuth.
evidence.quote: You must also complete a security questionnaire addressing questions of encryption, access controls, and token lifecycle management relating to OAuth token access.

evidence.claim: Privately distributed OAuth apps can be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts, not counting developer test accounts; static token apps are limited to one standard account.
evidence.quote: Privately distributed OAuth apps: can be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts (not including developer test accounts).

evidence.claim: Certification OAuth rules: users may only be asked to grant access (no copy-pasting codes or tokens), the app must handle token request and refresh without user involvement, and the app must call the Uninstall App endpoint when a customer removes it.
evidence.quote: Asking users to copy and paste OAuth codes or tokens is prohibited.

evidence.claim: Certification reliability threshold: average API success rate must be above 95% across activities, and error responses count against it; apps must also keep error responses under 5% of daily requests.
evidence.quote: Maintain an average success rate above **95%** across all [activities](#activity).

evidence.claim: Certification review: HubSpot responds to certification requests within 10 business days and the full review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared; HubSpot can reject a request at its discretion and an unsuccessful app may re-apply after six months.
evidence.quote: HubSpot can reject an app certification request at their discretion if it doesn't meet the set standards.

evidence.claim: Certification is free (no listing or certification fee, no revenue share). Certified status lasts two years and must be renewed; the app gets a certified badge and search filter once approved.
evidence.quote: No, we do not charge you a fee to list or certify your apps in the HubSpot Marketplace, nor a fee for installs generated through the HubSpot Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Certified apps are valid on a rolling two-year basis and must be renewed; HubSpot sends notices 90 days before the renewal date.
evidence.quote: App certifications are valid on a rolling basis for two years, and must be renewed.

evidence.claim: Sensitive Data scopes (for example crm.objects.contacts.sensitive.read) require Enterprise accounts; marketplace OAuth apps on 2025.2 or 2026.03 must request these from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, which allowlists them for testing before publication.
evidence.quote: you'll need to request access to specific sensitive scopes from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team.

evidence.claim: Sensitive scopes are separate read and write scopes per object (contacts, companies, deals, appointments, custom objects, projects, and tickets), and highly sensitive scopes are a second tier on top of them.
evidence.quote: If you want to access Highly Sensitive Data, you'll need additional scopes.

evidence.claim: After a marketplace app adds sensitive scopes, existing users must re-authorize, and a Super Admin in an Enterprise account must click the authorization URL to install with the new scopes.
evidence.quote: If they're existing users of the app, they'll need to reauthorize with the updated scopes for Sensitive Data access to apply.

evidence.claim: The Sensitive Data feature requires an account on an Enterprise subscription.
evidence.quote: The HubSpot account must have an Enterprise subscription to access Sensitive Data functionality.

evidence.claim: Agent tools listed on the Marketplace must not request sensitive data scopes at this time.
evidence.quote: at this time, your app must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: Changelog: apps created or migrated to Developer Platform 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until listed on the Marketplace, effective September 22, 2025; partners may instead distribute privately via OAuth to up to 10 customers (100 for Solution Partners).
evidence.quote: apps that are created or migrated to version 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until they are listed on the HubSpot Marketplace.

evidence.claim: App cards built with UI extensions must not access or request sensitive data scopes and must not display sensitive information.
evidence.quote: Your app must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: A community post says HubSpot's May 2026 certification review requires one API call per declared scope in the trailing 30 days; this is not on the official certification page, which says extraneous scopes must be removed.
Per-account rate limit for marketplace OAuth apps on 2025.2 or 2026.03 is 110 requests every 10 seconds per installing account (CRM Search excluded); the API limit increase add-on does not raise it.
evidence.quote: each HubSpot account that installs your app is limited to 110 requests every 10 seconds.

evidence.claim: Privately distributed apps have per-app burst limits of 100 per 10 seconds on Free/Starter, 190 on Professional/Enterprise, and 250 with the API Limit Increase; daily caps are shared per account.
evidence.quote: The burst limit, detailed in the Per 10 seconds column below, applies individually per app.

evidence.claim: Legacy private app creation was disabled on September 28, 2026 for new accounts and is disabled on October 26, 2026 for existing accounts; as of today (October 28, 2026) new legacy private apps cannot be created, and existing ones keep working until September 2027. Service Keys in Projects 2026.09 are the replacement.
evidence.quote: HubSpot is disabling new legacy private app creation starting September 28, 2026 for new accounts and October 26, 2026 for existing accounts.

evidence.claim: HubSpot is ending support for v1-v3 APIs, legacy public apps, and legacy private apps with September 2027 enforcement; public apps created before June 23, 2026 use the pre-Projects architecture and must move to Projects-based apps.
evidence.quote: HubSpot is ending support for v1-v3 APIs, legacy public apps, and legacy private apps, with September 2027 enforcement.

evidence.claim: Create an app with the CLI: run hs project create, choose the distribution (Marketplace or restricted to specific accounts) and auth (OAuth or static token); CLI v7.6.0 is the stated minimum for the 2025.2/2026.03 platform.
evidence.quote: Make sure you're using v7.6.0 of the HubSpot CLI before proceeding.

evidence.claim: Client ID and client secret are found by running hs project open, opening the project's app component, and copying values from the Auth tab's Client credentials section.
evidence.quote: Under Client credentials, copy the Client ID and Client secret from your new app

evidence.claim: The app's OAuth configuration (redirect URLs, requiredScopes, optionalScopes, conditionallyRequiredScopes) lives in app-hsmeta.json; for private static-token apps the redirectUrls field is removed.
evidence.quote: Add one or more valid redirect URLs to the app-hsmeta.json file based on your local (or another non-production) OAuth server configuration.

evidence.claim: Unlisted marketplace OAuth apps show an unverified-app warning at install; the installer must type an acceptance phrase before connecting.
evidence.quote: If your app has not yet been verified by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team, a warning banner will appear to alert the user that the app is unverified

evidence.claim: Redirect URLs are changed by editing the redirectUrls field in app-hsmeta.json and running hs project upload; the client secret can be rotated from the Auth tab.
evidence.quote: You can update these URLs by updating the redirectUrls field in your app's top-level app-hsmeta.json file, then running hs project upload.

evidence.claim: Redirect URI rules: must use https in production (http is allowed for localhost testing), must use a domain name (IP addresses not supported), and must match exactly what is registered.
evidence.quote: For security reasons, this URL must use https in production. (When testing using localhost, http can be used.)

evidence.claim: Scopes are checked in app-hsmeta.json or on the Auth tab; any scope marked required must appear in the scope parameter or the authorize page returns an error; optional scopes are dropped for accounts without access.
evidence.quote: Any scopes that you've checked off in your app's Auth settings will be treated as required

evidence.claim: Authorize URL is https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize (optionally with account ID in the path) taking client_id, scope, redirect_uri, optional_scope and state; the token exchange is a POST to /oauth/v3/token with grant_type authorization_code.
evidence.quote: You'll then make an API request to /oauth/v3/token with a request body that includes the code

evidence.claim: Access tokens include an expires_in value; a 401 response is not a valid signal to fetch a new access token, so apps must refresh based on expiry.
evidence.quote: Unauthorized (401) requests are not a valid indicator that a new access token must be retrieved.

evidence.claim: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes and are used with a refresh token to get a new access token (legacy OAuth v3 quickstart).
evidence.quote: This token is provided as a Bearer token in the request, and expires after 30 minutes.

evidence.claim: Apps are not shown as a Connected App in a user's account until the refresh and initial access tokens are generated.
evidence.quote: Your app will not appear as a Connected App in a user's account unless you generate the refresh token and initial access token.

evidence.claim: Test installs: a developer test account can be created under Development > Test accounts; add a test install from the project's Distribution tab; the installer must tick the unverified-app checkbox to connect.
evidence.quote: select the checkbox to authorize installing an unverified app, then click Connect app.

evidence.claim: Standard-account install is available from the Distribution tab under Standard install, requiring Super Admin or Marketplace access.
evidence.quote: On the Distribution tab, under Standard install, click Install now.

evidence.claim: Before installing a marketplace OAuth app in accounts other than developer test accounts, the developer must review and sign the Acceptable Use Policy from the Distribution tab via 'Begin publishing'.
evidence.quote: Review and sign the Acceptable Use Policy (AUP). Until the AUP is signed, you won't be able to install your app in accounts other than developer test accounts.

evidence.claim: Verified domain: add the domain under the Domain page in Development, publish a DNS TXT record, and wait for verification (usually about an hour, up to 48 hours to propagate). Only one verified domain per developer account; without it, installers see an unverified banner.
evidence.quote: The verification process usually completes within an hour, but you may need to wait up to 48 hours for the new DNS information to propagate.

evidence.claim: Developers need a HubSpot account with access to the Development menu (developer account); the Projects and Test accounts pages live under Development.
evidence.quote: In your HubSpot account, navigate to Development.

evidence.claim: Community says HubSpot's listing-submit button is disabled until three active installs exist; a community reply says the installs must be OAuth installs, and a privately listed app with a shared OAuth install link can be used for testers.
Installing users must be a Super Admin, or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access plus the permission for each scope group the app requests.
evidence.quote: Users with the HubSpot Marketplace access permission along with any scope groups requested by the app

evidence.claim: Marketplace minimum requirements include OAuth as the only authorization method, a listing tied to the public app ID and OAuth client ID, a unique app per use case, and no redirect to another app.
evidence.quote: OAuth: your app must use OAuth as its sole authorization method.

evidence.claim: Marketplace listing requires at least three active, unique HubSpot production installs unaffiliated with the developer, counting OAuth API activity or signed webhook/card requests in the past 30 days.
evidence.quote: Active installs are the number of unique HubSpot production accounts, unaffiliated with your organization, showing successful app activity within the past 30 days.

evidence.claim: Other listing rules: the app must use every scope it requests at install and remove unused ones, agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement, avoid restricted industries and classic CRM cards, and run on a non-retired developer platform version.
evidence.quote: Your app must use all of the scopes that it requests during installation.

open_questions: Refresh token lifetime and PKCE support were not confirmed from HubSpot's current OAuth pages. Check these before relying on long-lived sessions.
The HubSpot scopes reference page was not fetched, so the full list of scopes needing separate approval beyond Sensitive Data scopes is unverified.
The official listing requirements do not say whether a demo video or screenshots are required for a plain Marketplace listing; the demo video is confirmed only for certification.
No official source gives an end-to-end timeline for a first listing beyond the 10-business-day initial review and 60-day feedback window.
Whether the 25-install unlisted cap applies to Composio's managed HubSpot app is not confirmed; it depends on which app's client ID is used.
The exact UI for allowlisting up to 10 private accounts was not in the findings; confirm in the Distribution tab.
Developer portal login pages were not directly checked; navigation paths come from HubSpot documentation text.
A Solutions Partner override to the 10-account private allowlist (up to 100) is reported in a community post and the 2025.2 changelog excerpt, but not confirmed on a fetched official page.
Projects 2026.09 features (user-level apps, Service Keys) appear in release notes but were not verified on an official page.
The Ecosystem Quality team's contact channel for sensitive scope requests was not given in the findings.
